item_verdicts.title: Replace the event-count drag/hold discriminator with a distance slop; under §S24-C the ONLY threshold the slash-vs-move classifier needs is a tiny hold slop
item_verdicts.why: Headline survives and is repo-verified: DuelScene.update really does read `const mouseMoving = this.mouseHoldActive && this.dragPoints.length < 4`; core/gesture.ts classifyGesture returns only slash|jump|launch|stab (never a move verb); Sim.applyStroke gates only on `stroke.points.length < TWO` and TRUNCATES to reach (`stroke.truncateTo(reachFor(...))`) — there is no minimum-slash-length and no range gate. §S24-C's build consequence A12.2 is quoted accurately ('classification cannot steal short/point-blank drags for movement... any drawn stroke = slash (reach-truncated)'), and the §S24-H 2026-08-12 verify block CONFIRMS and STRENGTHENS point-blank-attacks (damage resolves ON DRAW). DragDetect source verified verbatim (drag rectangle sized by SM_CXDRAG/SM_CYDRAG). BUT two mechanism claims are wrong at the code, and they break the proposed fix as written.
item_verdicts.correction: (a) `mouseMoving` does not gate the move COMMAND. Sim.setPlayerIntent issues an order only on the null→value EDGE (`if (moveTargetX != null && previous == null) this.issueMoveOrder(moveTargetX)`), and that edge fires on the FIRST update tick after pointerdown, when dragPoints.length === 1. So every drag whose down-point is farther than MOVE_DEADZONE_PX (25 world px, src/config/combat-sim.ts) from the player latches a full move order at stroke ONSET — the bug is broader than 'the first ≤3 move events feed moveTargetX'; conversely a genuinely point-blank drag is inside the 25 px deadzone and is never stolen. (b) A jittery hold does NOT 'cancel run after 4 events': dropping moveTargetX back to null does not clear the latched order — `playerMove` is cleared only on arrival or in applyStroke's slash branch (`this.playerMove = null; // a swing overrides a walk order`), so the run continues to the latched target for the whole drag. Therefore keying `mouseMoving` on cumulative displacement is NOT sufficient: the move command must be DEFERRED past the slop (never pass a non-null moveTargetX until the hold has proven sub-slop, or issue it only on a sub-slop pointerup) and/or the latched playerMove must be explicitly cancelled the moment displacement crosses the slop.

item_verdicts.title: Capture coalesced pointer samples via Phaser's exposed native event — getCoalescedEvents through Pointer.event
item_verdicts.why: The escape-hatch does not exist in this repo's engine. Phaser v3.90.0 MouseManager binds 'mousemove'/'mousedown'/'mouseup'/'mouseover'/'mouseout'/'wheel' (verified against phaserjs/phaser v3.90.0 src/input/mouse/MouseManager.js — no PointerEvent API, no getCoalescedEvents anywhere), and the cited Phaser Pointer docs declare `event` as the union `TouchEvent, MouseEvent, WheelEvent` — PointerEvent is not in it. So `(p.event as PointerEvent).getCoalescedEvents?.()` is ALWAYS undefined on desktop; the mandatory optional-chaining fallback fires 100% of the time and the change is a silent no-op that buys zero extra stroke samples. The MDN facts quoted are accurate (returns a sequence of PointerEvents, pointermove/pointerrawupdate only, 'Limited availability... not Baseline', secure-context only), but they cannot be reached through Phaser 3's pointer abstraction.
item_verdicts.correction: Salvage path if coalesced capture is still wanted: register your OWN `canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', ...)` on game.canvas (or a custom input plugin) alongside Phaser's mouse listeners and read getCoalescedEvents there — a materially larger change than the claimed one-line edit, so effort is not 'Low' and the ADOPT adjudication does not hold as written. Also note EncounterScene has NO 2048 cap (`if (this.dragging) this.dragPoints.push(...)`, unbounded), so 'keep the 2048 cap... apply identically in EncounterScene' misdescribes that scene.

item_verdicts.title: pointerrawupdate — skip it
item_verdicts.why: The MDN warning is verbatim accurate ('because listening to pointerrawupdate events can affect performance, you should add these listeners only if... For most use cases, other pointer event types should suffice'), the Sim really does run a fixed-Hz accumulator (FIXED_HZ throughout src/core/Sim.ts), strokes really are consumed only at pointerup (finishStroke → sim.applyStroke), and 'Phaser's InputManager doesn't listen to the event' is confirmed by the v3.90.0 MouseManager listener list. But the cited ledger ground has been overturned since the research ran.
item_verdicts.correction: Drop the '§S24-E 60 fps burst proof: pure 15 fps stepper with zero interpolation' justification. The §S24-H 'Verify-pass corrections (2026-08-12)' block states 'The 60 fps "4-frame content block" defence is VOID — that is a property of the capture (§00), not of the game', and correction #4 directs: 'model the dash as a constant-speed line-follow ~616 px/s @1080 (~274 world px/s)... build the Sim mover constant-speed at 60 Hz... Do NOT hand-author a 27/55 stepper into core.' The OG is no longer established as a zero-interpolation 15 fps stepper. REJECT still stands on the surviving grounds: pointerup-only consumption, fixed-Hz Sim, MDN's own performance advice, and the fact that Phaser 3.90 binds no pointer events at all (so pointerrawupdate would additionally require a bespoke DOM listener).

item_verdicts.title: $1/$P gesture recognizers do not apply — the net-displacement sector classifier is the correct shape
item_verdicts.why: Repo half is exact: classifyGesture computes `net = sub(last, first)`, `Math.atan2(Math.abs(net.y), Math.abs(net.x))` against DIAG_RAD from GESTURE_DIAG_DEG=45, then sign for stab and polylineLength vs LAUNCH_FLICK_MAX_LEN for launch/jump — a net-displacement sector classifier, no templates. The $P page confirms the substance verbatim: '$P does not represent gestures as ordered points (i.e., strokes), but as unordered point-clouds' and 'stroke number, order, and direction are all ignored'. REJECT is sound. Two attributions overreach.
item_verdicts.correction: (1) 'video-confirmed SYNTHESIS §5' overstates the source: SYNTHESIS.md's own confirmation row reads 'Gestures (slash/jump/launch/stab) | draw-line slash confirmed everywhere; jump seen in Trap Challenge; launch/stab NOT isolable at 0.4 fps | ✅ PARTIAL visual confirmation'. Only slash is confirmed everywhere; the down=stab and up-flick=launch sectors are unconfirmed on film. (2) The cited pdollar.html page does not contain the clockwise-vs-counterclockwise caveat — it presents direction-invariance as a design property, not a stated limitation; cite the ICMI paper or drop the attribution.

item_verdicts.title: LAUNCH_FLICK length-as-speed proxy: real per-point timestamps are now cheap, but measure the OG's launch discrimination first
item_verdicts.why: Every checkable part holds. src/config/gesture.ts carries the exact comment 'Length proxies flick speed: raw pointer points carry no per-point timestamps in our pipeline' with LAUNCH_FLICK_MAX_LEN = 75 (annotated 'WORLD SPACE (SESSION13 A0)... Was 90 stage'), while RESUME_HERE.md decision #9 still reads `LAUNCH_FLICK_MAX_LEN=90` with default 'keep, revisit at Stage 2 feel pass' — the staleness flag is real and verified. 'The OG's launch-vs-jump rule has never been measured' also holds: COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md contains zero occurrences of flick/launch/up-stroke, and SYNTHESIS records launch as 'not isolable at 0.4 fps'. The {x,y,t} implementation note survives the Phaser finding that kills item 2, because Event.timeStamp exists on MouseEvent too (and Phaser's Pointer carries moveTime) — only the 'including each coalesced event' clause is unreachable here. One aside to discount: the note's 'the sector MAP is what's video-confirmed' inherits the same overstatement corrected in item 4 (slash confirmed; jump seen once; launch/stab not isolable), which if anything strengthens MEASURE_FIRST.

item_verdicts.title: Touch-vs-mouse unification: Phaser's pointer abstraction already covers it; only the slop constant would branch if touch becomes a target
item_verdicts.why: The ALREADY_DONE is real: DuelScene.create binds this.input.on('pointerdown'/'pointermove'/'pointerup') plus 'pointerupoutside' with the comment "Off-canvas releases emit 'pointerupoutside' — both must finish the stroke or it is silently swallowed (Stage-1 audit finding)", and EncounterScene binds the same four. Phaser does unify mouse and touch behind one Pointer. The future-adaptation note is factually wrong for the pinned engine.
item_verdicts.correction: 'branch on pointerType (available on the native event)' does not work in Phaser 3.90: MouseManager binds mousemove/mousedown/mouseup and Pointer.event is documented as `TouchEvent, MouseEvent, WheelEvent` — a MouseEvent has no pointerType. If a touch build ever happens, branch on Phaser's own Pointer flags (`p.wasTouch` / `p.pointerType` on the Phaser Pointer, not on `p.event`).

overall_note: Three of six items take real damage, and two share one root cause the research never checked: Phaser 3.90 does not use PointerEvents at all (MouseManager binds mousemove/mousedown/mouseup; Pointer.event is documented TouchEvent|MouseEvent|WheelEvent). That REFUTES the getCoalescedEvents-via-Pointer.event item outright (silent no-op, always falls back) and breaks the pointerType note in the touch item. Item 1's headline (distance slop over event count, ANY stroke = slash at any range) survives and is repo- and ledger-verified, but its stated failure mechanism is wrong: the move order is latched on the null→value EDGE at pointerdown (before any dragPoints exist) and nulling moveTargetX never cancels it — so the proposed one-line displacement swap would not fix the reported bug without deferring the command past the slop and/or cancelling the latched playerMove. Item 3's REJECT survives but must stop citing §S24-E's '60 fps burst / pure 15 fps stepper' — the §S24-H 2026-08-12 verify block voids that defence (post-dates the research, not the agent's fault). A cross-cutting sourcing correction: 'the video-confirmed 4-sector gesture map' overstates SYNTHESIS.md, which records slash confirmed everywhere, jump seen once, and launch/stab NOT isolable at 0.4 fps. Sources spot-checked live: MS DragDetect (supports), MDN getCoalescedEvents (supports), MDN pointerrawupdate (supports), UW $P page (supports point-cloud/direction-ignoring, does NOT contain the cw/ccw caveat), Phaser Pointer API docs + phaser v3.90.0 MouseManager source (contradict the item-2 mechanism). No dead or fabricated URLs found.
